gap: No result ChatGPT got works out what the two added screens cost a laptop on battery. The Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro draws 11 W from the laptop it is plugged into (CHIP.pl spec table). On its own, that draw would empty a 13-inch MacBook Air's 53.8 Wh battery in about 4.9 hours (53.8 ÷ 11). The extender also weighs about 1.5 times as much as that laptop (4.13 lb ÷ 2.7 lb).
standout_why: I compared against three pages. UPERFECT's cited blog lists weight, resolution and price for 8 extenders but gives no power draw and no battery figure. The Office Journal gives a 3.0 lb weight for one listing, says two panels draw 'meaningfully more power', and gives no wattage. Our own page (dealectric.com/best-triple-laptop-screen-extender) already has the Trio's 11 W and 4.13 lb, plus pixels per lb, price per sq in and price per megapixel for the Trio, UPERFECT, Xebec, FOPO S788 and Cevaton Z2. None of the three turns the 11 W into hours of laptop battery. Our page has no derived figures for the four FOPO dual extenders under $400 (S1, S7, S9G, S11). The ChatGPT answers give only resolution and price. PCWorld, Graded Picks, LaptopBee and DeskFinds were not opened.
decides: This confirms the Trio 3 Pro or UPERFECT BE14BF as the pick for sharpness: they add 6.27 MP against 4.61 MP for a 1920×1200 pair, 36% more. It qualifies that pick for unplugged use. The Trio's 11 W draw by itself takes 4.9 h of a 13-inch Air's battery (6.0 h of a 15-inch Air's), and Macworld and CHIP.pl both say laptop power alone can't reach full brightness. On price per added megapixel, our FOPO S7 ($43.40/MP) and S1 ($38.58/MP) beat the Trio ($58.67/MP) at today's store prices. That makes them the honest value segment for desk use, and the Trio the sharpness pick. Both FOPO rows have the same caveat: each screen needs its own video connection.
